description: Harvest-sustainability notes shown in Collapse Mode. Overharvest in year one starves you in year two.

records.note: Low density on the Shield (about 1 per 2–4 km²). Take bulls, leave cows and calves: one cow is the next decade's moose. One adult gives ~200 kg of meat.
Scarce in the far north, common in central Ontario. Deep-snow winters kill many: hunt bucks, protect deer yards in late winter.
Valuable fat (rendered for cooking and preserving). Slow to reproduce: take few, avoid sows with cubs. Cook bear meat thoroughly (trichinosis).
Populations boom and crash on a ~10-year cycle. In crash years, snare far less. Hare alone is too lean to live on (protein poisoning): pair with fat.
Easy to take, easy to over-harvest near camp. Spread hunting out over a wide area.
Fatty, high-calorie meat. Take 1–2 per colony per year at most; colonies maintain the ponds that hold fish, waterfowl and moose browse.
Spring and fall migrations bring surplus. Do not disturb nesting birds or take eggs from every nest.
Spawning runs in spring are easy pickings and the worst time to harvest: protect spawning shoals.
Very slow-growing in cold Shield lakes; a few seasons of heavy fishing can collapse a lake for decades. Treat as a reserve.
Abundant and resilient; take smaller pike and release large breeders.
Fall spawners in shallows: historically netted and dried for winter. Take part of the run, not all of it.
Small streams hold few fish: easily wiped out. Rotate streams.
